# Split previews paint the resulting region, not just the insertion line

## Context

Operator comparison study (2026-08-30): `webdock` — a compact dock prototype (~4.5k LOC) built by a single Opus 5 agent in under two hours — feels like it offers "more drop spots" and a smarter drag UX (light-blue regions instead of hunting icons). Both codebases were read and the engine was probed live before this ticket; the finding is sharper than the premise.

Live latest-open sweep: checked latest 15 open issues at 2026-08-30T00:20Z; no equivalent found. A2A claim sweep over the herd window: no competing claim (Euclid's PR #17869 owns #17865 — disjoint surface).

## The Problem

**The hit models are already equivalent.** Probed with a held synthetic gesture on the workstation at merged dev:

- Our `PreviewProducer#resolvePlacementKind` IS webdock's `zoneOf`: nearest-edge bands (`edgeBandRatio: 0.24` vs their `EDGE_FRACTION = 0.25`), tab-into center, the tab-header carve-out, indicator override on top, release-truth commit through the same payload path — one producer feeds preview AND commit in both codebases. A drop 25px inside a pane body (no icon anywhere near) **commits the inferred split today**; region drops are not missing.
- At a pane **center**, our preview already paints the full-zone translucent fill (`rgba(94, 234, 212, 0.2)` at the probed 414×543 zone) — exactly webdock's region language.

**The one real gap is the split-placement preview geometry.** In the edge bands, our affordance collapses to a **6px solid insertion line** at the zone edge (measured live: `w: 6, h: 543`) — the "green bars" of the report — while webdock's `edgePreview()` paints **the half-pane region the new pane would occupy** (`width * 0.5` along the direction). A thin line at the far edge of a pane is easy to miss and reads as "only the icons are interactive"; a half-pane fill is unmistakable and shows the *outcome*, not the *cut*. The perceived "must hit the icons exactly" is an affordance-legibility problem, not a hit-model problem — users gravitate to the icons because the icons are the only *legible* target, even though every pane pixel already works.

**Secondary gap — root-edge reachability:** webdock resolves the container's outer edges as hover *bands* (`containerEdgeSize` px along the full border) in addition to its edge markers; our root edges are reachable only through the 26px chips (`chipSize`). A band along the whole container border is a dramatically larger Fitts target for "dock across the full surface".

**Also observed (not this ticket's scope):** `examples/dashboard/dock` composes no affordance tier at all — a held drag over it paints nothing (no preview element, no indicators) while the drop still commits via inference. Silent-but-working; whether the minimal example should stay minimal is a separate call.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.mjs` — the renderer that maps a `dockPreview.v1` placement onto the affordance rect; the split/edge kinds currently resolve to the insertion-line geometry.
- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/PreviewProducer.mjs` — placement vocabulary (`split-before/after`, `edge-*`, `tab-into`); `produce()` is the pointer-inference tier; root chips come from `produceCandidates` only (no root band inference).
- `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss` — the `--dock-preview-*`/accept tokens; the region fill exists for tab-into and needs a split-region sibling.
- webdock reference points (read in full): `src/interaction/drop-resolver.js` (`zoneOf`, `containerEdge`, `edgePreview`), `src/interaction/drop-overlay.js` (`wd-drop-preview` region + active-dot highlight).

## The Fix

1. **Region previews for split placements (the adoption):** the Preview renderer maps `split-before/after` and `edge-*` to the RESULT region — the half of the target zone (or root) the new pane would occupy along the placement axis — painted with the translucent fill, keeping the current insertion line as the region's leading-edge accent (region communicates the outcome; the line still marks the exact cut). Tokenized fill/line so themes tune both.
2. **Optionality:** a reactive config on the Preview renderer (proposed: `resultRegionPreviews_: true`) with the current line-only presentation as the `false` branch — the operator floated the knob, and the pre-region look stays one config away. Default ON: at the pane center we already paint regions, so region-for-splits is consistency, not a new mode.
3. **Root-edge band inference (the secondary adoption):** `produce()` gains the container-edge fall-through — a pointer within a band (proposed: the chip inset geometry generalized, e.g. 24px) of the root rect's border resolves the `edge-*` root placement even between chips, mirroring webdock's `containerEdge` tier order (after indicator override, before zone inference at the border strip).
4. Witnesses: unit tier for the renderer's kind→rect mapping and the root-band inference (mutation-checked); the rendered component tier extends the live-preview spec with one region-visibility case (affordance rect ≈ half-zone for a band hover).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Hovering a pane's edge band (no indicator) paints the half-zone result region with the insertion line as its leading edge; the pane center keeps the full-zone fill.
- [ ] `resultRegionPreviews: false` restores the line-only presentation (both states witnessed).
- [ ] Hovering within the root-edge band between chips resolves and previews the root `edge-*` placement; the chips continue to work unchanged.
- [ ] No commit-semantics change: `previewToOperation` payloads are byte-identical for every placement kind (the change is presentation + one added inference tier, witnessed by unchanged unit expectations on produced payloads).
- [ ] Tokens documented in the theme block; the **workstation** renders sanely with engine defaults. The minimal example composes no affordance tier (see *Out of scope*), so it has no affordance to render — its sanity is not evidence this ticket can produce. *(Corrected 2026-08-30 by @neo-opus-ada under an operator-directed takeover of PR #17873; rationale and revert offer in the comment thread.)*

## Out of Scope

- The minimal example's missing affordance tier (separate call, noted above).
- Tab-strip insertion carets for cross-zone index-precise inserts (webdock has them; our cross-zone tab-into appends — a different, larger vocabulary question).
- Any hit-model change to pane-body inference (already equivalent).

## Avoided Traps

- Copying webdock's model wholesale: its strengths we lack are two bounded features; its architecture (single-window, no worker boundary, no committed document) does not transplant. The comparison's real lesson is visual: **show the outcome region, not the cut line.**
- Replacing the insertion line: the line carries exact-cut information the region blurs; the adoption keeps both.

## Decision Record impact

aligned-with ADR 0029 (presentation-only preview tier; the committed document stays the sole size authority).
